"""Layer 15, MLP down_proj, component 4480: a word-class sign detector.

The component's activation is mostly negative on nouns, and most negative on
generic technical head nouns and nouns for made things. It reads only the
newest token (and the one before it, for context), so each prediction is
causal.

- Common nouns for ordinary things are mildly negative.
- Nouns for made things, methods and abstract constructs are more negative
  (WordNet lexicographer classes: artifact, act, cognition, communication,
  food, shape, object, plant, phenomenon, group, possession, event, state).
- Generic technical head nouns are most negative: system, method, model,
  function, process, approach, solution, problem, equation, algorithm, data.
- Nouns right after a determiner or adjective ("the method", "a dataset")
  are more negative, since they open a noun phrase. Nouns after a noun
  (compounds) are less negative.
- Rare nouns (Zipf frequency below 4.5) are more negative than common ones
  (Zipf frequency 5.5 and up), which are mildly positive.
- Adjectives and verbs are mildly positive; capitalised words are positive.
- Pieces of a longer word (no leading space) are mildly negative.
- Punctuation, digits and spaces are zero.

The weights were fit by least squares on about a million training tokens and
rounded. Prediction on held-out training rows: variance explained about 0.07.
The program has no state.
"""
import wordfreq
import wordnet

READS = ()

DETERMINERS = {"the", "a", "an", "this", "that", "these", "those", "his", "her",
               "their", "its", "my", "your", "our", "such", "one", "some", "each",
               "every", "any", "no"}
MADE_THINGS = {"noun.artifact", "noun.act", "noun.cognition", "noun.communication",
               "noun.food", "noun.shape", "noun.object", "noun.plant",
               "noun.phenomenon", "noun.group", "noun.possession", "noun.event",
               "noun.state"}
GENERIC = {"system", "systems", "method", "methods", "model", "models", "function", "functions",
           "process", "processes", "approach", "approaches", "solution", "solutions", "problem",
           "problems", "equation", "equations", "formula", "formulas", "algorithm", "algorithms",
           "program", "programs", "study", "studies", "question", "questions", "project", "projects",
           "plan", "plans", "mechanism", "mechanisms", "technique", "techniques", "procedure",
           "procedures", "strategy", "framework", "structure", "device", "devices", "tool", "tools",
           "data", "information", "file", "files", "code", "table", "list", "line", "name", "term",
           "case", "point", "points", "number", "value", "unit", "set", "sequence", "element",
           "matrix", "graph"}

# Weights, in activation units.
NOUN = -0.13
MADE = -0.3
GENERIC_NOUN = -1.5
AFTER_DET_OR_ADJ = -0.5
AFTER_NOUN = -0.1
RARE_NOUN = -0.35
COMMON_NOUN = 0.55
ADJECTIVE = 0.15
VERB = 0.2
CAPITALISED = 0.37
WORD_PIECE = -0.2


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    text = word.strip().lower()
    same_doc = len(prefix.token_strings) > 1 and prefix.document_ids[-2] == prefix.document_ids[-1]
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2].strip().lower() if same_doc else ""
    value = 0.0
    if text.isalpha() and word[:1] == " ":
        pos = wordnet.parts_of_speech(text)
        if "noun" in pos:
            value += NOUN
            if wordnet.categories(text) & MADE_THINGS:
                value += MADE
            if text in GENERIC:
                value += GENERIC_NOUN
            if prev in DETERMINERS or "adjective" in wordnet.parts_of_speech(prev):
                value += AFTER_DET_OR_ADJ
            if prev and "noun" in wordnet.parts_of_speech(prev):
                value += AFTER_NOUN
            zipf = wordfreq.zipf_frequency(text, "en")
            if zipf < 4.5:
                value += RARE_NOUN
            elif zipf >= 5.5:
                value += COMMON_NOUN
        elif "adjective" in pos:
            value += ADJECTIVE
        elif "verb" in pos:
            value += VERB
        if word.strip()[:1].isupper():
            value += CAPITALISED
    elif text.isalpha():
        value += WORD_PIECE
    return carry, float(value)

"""Weak layout offset for component p-82af68dd@100000/layers.15.mlp.down_proj:4481.

The component is almost exactly MLP hidden unit 4481 of layer 15 (it reads that unit with
weight 0.86). Its activation is near zero on most tokens and takes both signs, with large
values in rare places: aligned tables, code, lists, math layouts. No token identity, bigram,
document-level or short-context feature we tried predicts it (variance explained about 0).

The one tendency measured: it is a little more positive on newline tokens (mean +0.09 vs
-0.02 overall) and on whitespace tokens (mean +0.01), and slightly negative on words and
punctuation. This program predicts those small offsets and nothing more.
"""

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

NEWLINE = 0.09
SPACES = 0.01
OTHER = -0.01


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    s = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if "\n" in s:
        value = NEWLINE
    elif s and s.strip() == "":
        value = SPACES
    else:
        value = OTHER
    return carry, value

"""Layer 15 MLP down-projection, component 4482: a "logical link" detector.

The component is high on words that join one clause or state to another by
cause, consequence, contrast, condition or timing ("therefore", "thus", "hence",
"because", "so", "however", "although", "unless", "before", "when"), and on verbs
that say one thing causes, means, implies, enables or prevents another ("makes",
"means", "suggests", "ensures", "prevents", "allows", "requires"). Its strongest
readings are on connectives, and its output pushes the model toward pronouns
("its", "their", "they") as the next word.

It is mildly negative on coordinating and question words ("and", "or", "which",
"what", "how") and on hedges and fillers ("maybe", "hmm", "possibly", "wait"),
and sits near its mean (about 0.1) everywhere else.

The program reads only the newest token, so it has no carry and no context.
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

# Words that link two clauses or states by cause, consequence, contrast or condition.
CONNECTIVES = set(
    "therefore thus hence because so consequently thereby accordingly however "
    "despite unless although though but yet whereas 但 但是 因此 所以 porque pero mais wenn".split()
)
# Words of time sequence and reason, which also join clauses.
TIMING = set("when while before after until since once then if during without otherwise than why reason due".split())
# Verbs that say one thing causes, means, implies, enables, requires or prevents another.
CAUSAL_VERBS = set(
    "make makes made making means mean meant meaning suggests suggest suggesting "
    "indicates indicate implies imply ensure ensures prevent prevents allow allows "
    "enable enables affect affects protect avoid cause causes caused lead leads led "
    "leading requires require creates increases increase improve keep keeping maintain "
    "depending determine represents render".split()
)
# Coordinating and question words, which lean the other way.
NEGATIVE = set("and or which what how".split())
# Hedges and fillers, which lean further the other way.
HEDGES = set("maybe possibly hmm hope wait actually even finally again here".split())

BASE = 0.1  # the component's typical value on ordinary tokens


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    if word in CONNECTIVES:
        return carry, 2.3
    if word in CAUSAL_VERBS:
        return carry, 1.25
    if word in TIMING:
        return carry, 0.9
    if word in NEGATIVE:
        return carry, -0.25
    if word in HEDGES:
        return carry, -0.3
    return carry, BASE

"""Person-reference detector for component 4483 of layer 15's MLP down_proj.

What the component is: its input direction reads mostly MLP hidden unit 4483 of
layer 15 (about 40% of the input vector's energy), so the activation is roughly that
unit's value. It is dense and context-driven: most of its variance is not explained by
any single word. Its clearest spikes come where the text names a person acting in some
role (an author, owner, examiner, developers, researchers, parents, a member), and on
the word right after a title ("Mr", "Dr", "Professor"). It goes mildly negative on
subject pronouns ("I", "we", "he").

What this program does: it looks only at the newest token (no state). It predicts a
baseline of the component's average value, raised for role nouns and for the word after
a title, and lowered for subject pronouns. It captures very little of the variance; see
the explanation for what would be needed to do better.
"""

import inflect

READS = ()

BASELINE = 0.03  # the component's average activation over the eval rows

# Role or occupation nouns that name a person acting in some role (singular forms).
ROLE_NOUNS = set("""
author owner examiner teacher writer reader developer manager lawyer judge doctor
moderator reviewer officer father mother parent researcher interpreter speaker user
customer student employee editor creator sponsor supervisor assistant technician
designer artist expert programmer professional consumer coach player friend
""".split())

TITLES = {"mr", "mrs", "ms", "dr", "prof", "professor", "sir", "madam"}
SUBJECT_PRONOUNS = {"i", "we", "he", "she", "they"}

_inflect = inflect.engine()


def _singular(word):
    """The singular of a plural noun, or the word itself."""
    singular = _inflect.singular_noun(word)
    return singular if singular else word


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    previous = prefix.token_strings[-2].strip().lower() if len(prefix.token_strings) > 1 else ""
    if word in SUBJECT_PRONOUNS:
        return carry, BASELINE - 0.15
    if word.isalpha() and (word in ROLE_NOUNS or _singular(word) in ROLE_NOUNS):
        return carry, BASELINE + 0.6
    if previous in TITLES:
        return carry, BASELINE + 0.4
    return carry, BASELINE

"""Layer 15 MLP, the component's activation is mostly MLP hidden unit 4484:
silu(gate) * up for that unit, which accounts for about two-thirds of the
component's variance (the rest is spread over many units).

What the unit does: its value is a heavy tail of large negative values (down to
-30) that no simple token class, bigram, repetition, character-class, or
word-frequency rule predicts (held-out R^2 below 0.01 for all of them).
Gate and up are each about 11% predictable from the current token, but their
product is not. Large negatives come from gate near +5 with up near -2 to -3.

What this program does: it predicts only the stable part. The unit is silent
(0) on a document's first token, is noisy and mildly negative over the next few
tokens, and is near zero, slightly positive, afterwards. It explains almost
none of the variance (about 0.07% on eval). The tail is left out; a table of
token values would not add much (held-out R^2 about 0.4%).
"""

READS = ()

EARLY = 4          # positions 1..3 of a document
EARLY_VALUE = -0.18
LATE_VALUE = 0.03


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # carry: (document id of the previous token, position within its document)
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        pos = 0
    else:
        pos = carry[1] + 1
    if pos == 0:
        value = 0.0
    elif pos < EARLY:
        value = EARLY_VALUE
    else:
        value = LATE_VALUE
    return (doc, pos), float(value)

"""Layer 15 MLP, down_proj component 4485: a constant predictor.

What the component is: its activation is (x . V_c) * ||U_c|| on the MLP hidden state x. V_c is
0.60 on hidden unit 4485 of layer 15 and 0.16 or less on any other unit, and ||U_c|| = 0.90.
So the activation is essentially hidden unit 4485 scaled by about 0.54; that unit accounts for
~44% of the activation's variance on our sample.

What we found: the value is not carried by any token or surface property we could name.
- Per-token means explain ~1% of its variance out of sample; previous-token bigram means ~1.6%.
- Character-class windows (CJK, Cyrillic, digits, punctuation, whitespace) and English word
  frequency explain ~0%.
- Position in a document is weak: the second token averages 0.15, most others about 0.06.
- Model surprisal and next-token entropy do not correlate with it (|r| < 0.03).
- Its values are mostly small (std ~0.37) with rare large excursions in both signs.

So the readable program predicts the component's typical value everywhere. It captures none of
its variance (eval variance explained ~0) and leaves the model's outputs where switching the
component off does (eval kl_fraction ~0.97).
"""

READS = ()

TYPICAL = 0.06
"""The component's mean activation over training text (about 0.065 on 2M tokens)."""


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    return carry, TYPICAL

"""Layer 15 MLP down_proj, component 4486: a weak, diffuse word-class feature.

What it does, in plain terms: the component's activation is small and noisy for most
tokens, and it is positive on words that add emphasis or signal a need or a call to
action ("also", "more", "most", "still", "very", "must", "need", "important", "continue"),
and negative on words about protection, safety and rights ("protect", "safety", "secure",
"guidelines", "rights", "criteria", "care", "court").

Its write side is readable: its output direction raises the logits of urgency words
("urgent", "danger", "warning", "alarm") when positive and of appreciation words
("fascination", "interest", "love", "fun") when negative. The read side is only loosely
tied to that: the activation is higher in persuasive, civic and advocacy prose and lower
in code, maths and technical text, but that context signal explains very little.

This program predicts the activation from the current token alone with three word lists
and a 0 for everything else. It explains under 1% of the variance (about 0.5% on eval).
Most of the variance sits in context this word-level view cannot reach.
"""

READS = ()

# Emphasis and addition: words that extend or intensify the point being made.
ADDITIVE = set("""also more most further furthermore moreover too much still plus additionally
especially particularly very truly highly significantly substantially simply definitely fully currently""".split())

# Necessity and call to action: words that set up an obligation or an action.
NECESSITY = set("""must need needs needed require required important critical continue remain
become join fight rise efforts actions committed immediately urgent""".split())

# Protection, safety and rights vocabulary: the component runs negative on these.
PROTECT = set("""protect protection safety safe secure guidance guidelines rights criteria care fraud court
immune diseases""".split())


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """The activation at this position, from the newest token alone (no state is carried)."""
    word = "".join(ch for ch in prefix.token_strings[-1].lower() if "a" <= ch <= "z")
    if word in ADDITIVE:
        value = 0.6
    elif word in NECESSITY:
        value = 0.5
    elif word in PROTECT:
        value = -0.6
    else:
        value = 0.0
    return carry, value

"""Early-document dip in layers.15.mlp.down_proj component 4488.

This component's activation is close to zero-mean noise at almost every token
(std about 0.8, with rare large spikes of either sign). Its spikes are not tied to
any token identity, bigram, or simple lexical property I could find: a per-token
lookup table only explains a few percent out of sample, and everything below is
much weaker than that.

The one regular effect is at the start of a document. The second, third and fourth
tokens of a document (positions 1, 2, 3, counting from 0 at the document's first
token) sit below the usual level, most strongly at position 1. Everywhere else the
program predicts the component's typical value, a small negative number.

The carry keeps the document label and the position within it, and resets at each
document change, as the model does.
"""

READS = ()

TYPICAL = -0.05  # the component's mean activation away from document starts
EARLY_DIP = {1: -0.66, 2: -0.38, 3: -0.22}  # mean activation at document positions 1-3


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or doc != carry[0]:
        pos = 0  # first token of a document
    else:
        pos = carry[1] + 1
    return (doc, pos), EARLY_DIP.get(pos, TYPICAL)

"""Question-asking speech in dialogue: a weak, dense feature of layers.15 mlp.down_proj, unit 4490.

What it does: most of the time the activation is near zero, with small noise. It runs
positive on speech that asks or addresses someone else. The clearest cases are inside
quoted speech (dialogue, interviews, chat): "you", wh-words ("What", "How", "Why"), question
marks, and the words of a sentence that opens like a question ("Have you...", "Did you...",
"How about you?"). Modals, first-person words and acknowledgements count a little there.
Outside quotes the same cues count for much less. Acknowledgements that open a sentence
("Good", "Okay", "Yeah") are slightly negative.

The program follows two states token by token: whether we are inside quoted speech, and
whether the current sentence opened with a question word or an auxiliary verb. It adds up
the weights of the cues in the current token. The weights are scaled down: the feature
is hard to predict from these cues, and full-size predictions hurt the fit.

On the eval rows it explains 0.3% of the activation's variance (r = 0.07), and it leaves
the model's next-token output almost unchanged. The rest is a diffuse context signal, and
most of the large values sit in contexts this program does not see.
"""

READS = ()

QUESTION_WORDS = {"what", "how", "why", "who", "whom", "where", "when", "which"}
AUXILIARIES = {"is", "are", "was", "were", "do", "does", "did", "can", "could", "will",
               "would", "should", "have", "has", "am"}
YOU_WORDS = {"you", "your", "yours", "you're", "you'll", "you've", "u"}
MODALS_AND_SELF = {"must", "should", "can", "will", "would", "could", "might",
                   "i", "i'm", "i'll", "i've", "me", "my"}
ACK_WORDS = {"good", "yes", "yeah", "okay", "ok", "thanks", "right", "perfect", "excellent",
             "sure", "well", "great", "cool", "alright", "see", "know"}
SENTENCE_END = ".!?\n。！？"

# weight of each cue: (inside quoted speech, outside quotes)
WEIGHTS = {
    "you": (0.4, 0.1),
    "wh_word": (0.25, 0.05),
    "question_mark": (0.2, 0.05),
    "question_sentence": (0.65, 0.3),
    "modal_or_self": (0.1, 0.0),
    "ack_word": (0.1, 0.0),
    "ack_opens_sentence": (-0.1, -0.1),
}


def _word(text):
    return text.strip().lower().strip(" ,.!?\"“”'")


def _fresh(doc):
    return {"doc": doc, "quote": False, "first": None, "question": False}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    text = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    c = carry if carry is not None and carry["doc"] == doc else _fresh(doc)
    word = _word(text)
    opens = c["first"] is None and bool(word)  # first word of a sentence
    if opens:
        c["first"] = word
        c["question"] = word in QUESTION_WORDS or word in AUXILIARIES
    if "“" in text:
        c["quote"] = True
    if "”" in text:
        c["quote"] = False
    if text.count('"') % 2 == 1:
        c["quote"] = not c["quote"]
    cues = {
        "you": word in YOU_WORDS,
        "wh_word": word in QUESTION_WORDS,
        "question_mark": text.strip()[:1] in ("?", "？"),
        "question_sentence": c["question"],
        "modal_or_self": word in MODALS_AND_SELF,
        "ack_word": word in ACK_WORDS,
        "ack_opens_sentence": opens and word in ACK_WORDS,
    }
    k = 0 if c["quote"] else 1
    value = sum(WEIGHTS[name][k] for name, on in cues.items() if on)
    if any(ch in SENTENCE_END for ch in text):
        c["first"] = None
        c["question"] = False
    return c, float(value)

"""Layer 15 MLP down_proj, component 4491: a diffuse readout that no simple rule predicts.

What the component reads: its input direction is almost entirely the MLP hidden unit
4491 of layer 15 (weight 0.22 of its 0.55 total norm; the other 6143 hidden units carry
small weights around 0.02 each). Its activation is that dot product scaled by the output
norm: std 0.30, mean 0, and it is not token-driven.

Why this program predicts 0 everywhere: over 4096 training rows (about 2M tokens) the
activation shows no structure we can name. Token identity, token class (word, punctuation,
digits, CJK, bytes, whitespace, newline), position in the document, repeated tokens, running
token-class densities and per-document means each explain about 0 held-out variance (R^2
below 0.001). Switched off, the component changes the model's next-token distribution by
about 1e-6 nats per position, so predicting 0 is close to switching it off.
"""

READS = ()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # The component has no readable rule: predict its mean, 0, at every position.
    return carry, 0.0

"""Layer 15, MLP hidden unit 4492 (this component is that unit, scaled by about 1.3).

The unit goes strongly negative on the tokens of headings, running headers and
page furniture: stretches of ALL-CAPS words, page numbers and digits, and line breaks
inside such text (OCR'd PDFs, exam papers, reports). Its large negative spikes are rare
and hard to predict from the text, so this program only gives the mild, average trend:
a small negative value for a digit, line break or capitalised word, scaled by the share
of ALL-CAPS words among the last 16 tokens. Everywhere else it predicts 0.
"""

READS = ()

WINDOW = 16  # recent tokens looked at for "heading-like" text
SCALE = -0.6  # average activation when the whole window is ALL-CAPS (fit on training rows)


def _is_caps_word(tok):
    word = tok.strip()
    return len(word) > 1 and word.isalpha() and word.isupper()


def _is_digit_or_break(tok):
    return tok.strip().isdigit() or "\n" in tok or "\\n" in tok


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # carry: (document id, flags of the last WINDOW tokens: 1 if ALL-CAPS word)
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        flags = []
    else:
        flags = carry[1]
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    caps_share = sum(flags) / len(flags) if flags else 0.0
    value = 0.0
    if _is_digit_or_break(tok) or _is_caps_word(tok):
        value = SCALE * caps_share
    flags = (flags + [1 if _is_caps_word(tok) else 0])[-WINDOW:]
    return (doc, flags), value

"""Layer 15 MLP down_proj, component 4493: a weak, mostly unexplained signal.

What it is: a single rank-one write into the residual stream. Its input direction is
dominated by MLP hidden unit 4493 of layer 15 (about a quarter of its weight energy), and
the rest is spread thinly over thousands of other hidden units. No simple feature of the
text predicts its size: the current token's identity, the previous token, the token's
script or class, its position, and even the whole document's average each explain
essentially none of its variance (held-out R^2 about 0).

What this program does: it encodes the one regularity found. A token that starts a
document (it has no earlier tokens to attend to) gives an activation of about 0. Every
other token gets the component's typical value, its mean, about 0.02. It predicts
no further detail, so it explains almost none of the variance and leaves the model's
output essentially unchanged, as switching the component off does.
"""

READS = ()

MEAN_ACTIVATION = 0.02  # the component's typical value away from document starts
DOCUMENT_START = 0.0    # near zero at the first token of a document


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    t = prefix.position
    starts_document = t == 0 or prefix.document_ids[t] != prefix.document_ids[t - 1]
    return carry, DOCUMENT_START if starts_document else MEAN_ACTIVATION

"""Layer 15, MLP down_proj, component 4494: a near-silent feature with no simple cause found.

What the component is: its activation is (MLP hidden vector . V_c) * ||U_c||. Its V_c is
about one-third concentrated on MLP hidden unit 4494 of layer 15, so the activation is
roughly 0.4 times that unit. That unit is strongly negative inside code, shell and markup
spans and mildly positive in some prose and reasoning text (" again", "Similarly").
Nothing simple predicts it from the text: token identity explains about 1% of its variance
on held-out rows, and recent-token averages, code-versus-prose density and the model's own
confidence explain nothing. The component is also almost never causally important (its CI
never passes 0.1 in 10 million tokens), so it barely changes the model's output.

What this program does: it predicts the component's average activation (about -0.025) at
every token, except 0 at the first token of each row or document, where the component is
silent. That is the best constant guess from the prefix, and it is all the text supports.
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

MEAN = -0.025
"""The component's average activation over ordinary tokens."""


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    starts_document = prefix.position == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    return carry, 0.0 if starts_document else MEAN

"""Layer 15 MLP down_proj, component 4495: a weak, mostly unexplained readout.

What the component is: its activation is (MLP hidden vector) . v, where v is the component's
input direction scaled by its output norm. The layer-15 MLP hidden unit 4495 itself accounts
for about a third of the activation's variance (its top examples include "Connecticut",
"Marshall", "soldier", "people", but also much noise); the rest is spread thinly over
thousands of hidden units. No token class, word type or context I could name predicts it:
token identity explains about 1-2% of its variance out of sample, and word categories ~0.1%.

What this program does: it predicts the small, stable pattern that is present:
  - the first token of each document is exactly 0 (the component is silent there);
  - the second token of a document is about +0.13;
  - the next few tokens are slightly negative (about -0.02);
  - everywhere else it sits at its typical value, about +0.025.
This explains well under 1% of the variance. Switching the component off changes the model's
next-token predictions by almost nothing (KL ~1e-6 nats), so this is a description, not a
mechanism. A token table would add a little more variance but is not a concept, so it is not used.
"""

READS = ()

DOC_START = 0.0  # first token of a document
SECOND = 0.13  # second token of a document
EARLY = -0.02  # tokens 2 to 9 of a document
TYPICAL = 0.025  # all other tokens


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # carry: (document label of the last token, index of the last token within its document)
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        index = 0
    else:
        index = carry[1] + 1
    if index == 0:
        value = DOC_START
    elif index == 1:
        value = SECOND
    elif index < 10:
        value = EARLY
    else:
        value = TYPICAL
    return (doc, index), value

What it does, in plain terms: this component writes a "you"-directed signal into the
residual stream (its output direction favours tokens like "you", "你", "您", "给您",
"帮你"). It is switched on most strongly where the text is in a first-person voice of a
speaker (an assistant, a company, a writer) who is about to say what they will do or
offer for the reader: "We hope ...", "I recommend ...", "we'll help ...", "Let me give
you ...", "we can make ...", "we provide ...".

The program models that as a running score over the text:
  * each word of the speaker's voice (I, we, me, us, my, our), of a future or modal
    (will, can, would, 'll ...) or of helping, offering or promising (help, provide,
    offer, recommend, hope, guarantee, ensure, give, make ...) adds +1;
  * the word "to" (as in "love to", "want to") adds +0.3;
  * past-tense narrative verbs (was, had, said, went, felt ...) subtract 0.3;
  * the score decays by half at each token, so it stays up for a few words after the
    trigger, and it resets at each document boundary.
Its prediction is a scaled, shifted copy of that score, with the scale and shift fitted
by least squares on sample text. It is a rough model: most of the component's variance
is contextual and not carried by any word list, so this captures only a small part.
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

SPEAKER = {"i", "we", "me", "us", "my", "our"}
MODAL = {"will", "can", "would", "could", "may", "should", "must", "ll"}
OFFER = {
    "help", "assist", "provide", "offer", "give", "deliver", "recommend", "suggest",
    "propose", "guarantee", "ensure", "ensures", "ensuring", "promise", "bring",
    "encourage", "tell", "show", "keep", "hope", "hoping", "want", "wants", "love",
    "expect", "expects", "confident", "sorry", "welcome", "make", "put", "take",
    "allow", "let", "share", "explain",
}
TO = {"to"}  # infinitive "to" after "love", "want", "hope": a weaker signal
PAST = {"was", "were", "had", "did", "said", "went", "felt", "saw", "got", "came",
        "looked", "replied", "thought"}
DECAY = 0.5  # how much of the score carries over to the next token
TO_WEIGHT = 0.3
PAST_WEIGHT = -0.3
SCALE = 0.8  # fitted on sample text: activation ~ SCALE * score + OFFSET
OFFSET = -0.03


def _word(text: str) -> str:
    """A token's word: lower case, no leading space, curly apostrophes made straight."""
    return text.strip().lower().replace("’", "'").strip("'")


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    trace, last_doc = carry if carry is not None else (0.0, None)
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if doc != last_doc:  # a new document starts: forget the earlier text
        trace = 0.0
    word = _word(prefix.token_strings[-1])
    if word in SPEAKER or word in MODAL or word in OFFER:
        x = 1.0
    elif word in TO:
        x = TO_WEIGHT
    elif word in PAST:
        x = PAST_WEIGHT
    else:
        x = 0.0
    trace = DECAY * trace + x
    return (trace, doc), SCALE * trace + OFFSET

"""Digit-context detector for layers.15.mlp.down_proj component 4522.

What the component does, in plain terms: it fires on digits that sit inside numbers.
Its activation is higher the more digits there are in the last few tokens (a dense
run of numbers, as in prices, measurements or tables), and higher still on a digit
that follows a decimal point or a currency sign ("$1", "0.5"). Digits that follow
word-like text are weaker, and ordinary words and punctuation sit slightly below zero.

This program predicts that pattern from the text alone. It explains only a small
share of the component's variance: most of its activation is not a function of the
current and recent tokens.
"""

import unicodedata
from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

WINDOW = 16
"""How many recent tokens (in the same document) count toward the digit density."""

LEAD_IN = {".", "$", "£", "€", "\\$", "≈", "~", "="}
"""Tokens after which a digit reads as a decimal or currency amount."""


def is_digit(text):
    """True for a token made only of digit characters (0-9 and other Unicode decimal digits)."""
    text = text.strip()
    return bool(text) and all(unicodedata.category(ch) == "Nd" for ch in text)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    t = prefix.position
    words = prefix.token_strings
    docs = prefix.document_ids
    now = words[t]
    if not is_digit(now):
        return carry, -0.06
    start = t
    while start > 0 and docs[start - 1] == docs[t] and t - start < WINDOW - 1:
        start -= 1
    recent = words[start : t + 1]
    density = sum(is_digit(w) for w in recent) / len(recent)
    value = 0.15 + 0.25 * density
    if t > 0 and docs[t - 1] == docs[t] and words[t - 1].strip() in LEAD_IN:
        value += 0.45
    return carry, value

What the component is: a single rank-one readout of layer 15's MLP hidden state. Its
activation is small and dense: mean about 0.03, spread about 0.3, on nearly every token.

"""Layer 15 MLP down_proj, component 4527: a negation detector for reasoning text.

Plain-language reading: this component is near zero almost everywhere. It turns
on where a claim is being denied, doubted or contrasted, mostly in argument and
reasoning text. Its strongest cue is a negation word right after a hedge or
discourse marker ("maybe not", "probably not", "might not", "so not",
"Wait not"). A negation after an auxiliary or copula ("is not", "does not",
"doesn't", "can't") is weaker, and a negation after anything else ("X, not Y",
"if not", "to not") is weaker still. The activation also stays raised for a few
tokens after a negation. Contrast words ("but", "however", "Wait", "Hmm") add a smaller amount.

The program predicts the activation as a weighted sum of these cues, with the
weights fitted by least squares on training text. It reads only earlier tokens,
within the same document.
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

NEGATION = {"not", "no", "never", "nothing", "none", "nobody", "nor", "neither",
            "cannot", "n't", "'t", "without", "nowhere"}
HEDGE = {"maybe", "probably", "might", "so", "still", "wait", "perhaps", "possibly",
         "likely", "→"}
AUXILIARY = {"is", "are", "was", "were", "be", "been", "does", "did", "would", "could",
             "might", "may", "can", "will", "should", "'s", "isn", "doesn", "wasn",
             "aren", "didn", "won", "wouldn"}
CONTRAST = {"but", "however", "although", "though", "nevertheless", "unless", "yet",
            "whereas", "instead", "wait", "hmm"}

BASE = 0.036          # typical activation with no cue
NEG_AFTER_HEDGE = 3.9
NEG_AFTER_AUX = 1.5
NEG_OTHER = 0.66
CONTRAST_W = 0.80
NEG_CONTEXT_W = 0.61  # decayed count of negations in the last 8 tokens
CONTRAST_CONTEXT_W = 0.14
DECAY = 0.6
WINDOW = 8


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    words = [s.strip().lower() for s in prefix.token_strings]
    docs = prefix.document_ids
    t = prefix.position
    cur = words[t]
    prev = words[t - 1] if t > 0 and docs[t - 1] == docs[t] else ""
    value = BASE
    if cur in NEGATION:
        if prev in HEDGE:
            value += NEG_AFTER_HEDGE
        elif prev in AUXILIARY:
            value += NEG_AFTER_AUX
        else:
            value += NEG_OTHER
    if cur in CONTRAST:
        value += CONTRAST_W
    neg_context = 0.0
    contrast_context = 0.0
    for k in range(1, min(WINDOW, t) + 1):
        if docs[t - k] != docs[t]:
            break
        weight = DECAY ** (k - 1)
        if words[t - k] in NEGATION:
            neg_context += weight
        if words[t - k] in CONTRAST:
            contrast_context += weight
    value += NEG_CONTEXT_W * neg_context + CONTRAST_CONTEXT_W * contrast_context
    return carry, float(value)

import re

READS = ()
DECAY = 0.6  # how much of the previous total survives one token

# Early-stage words, which give the strongest dip.
STRONG = re.compile(
    r"\s*(young\w*|early|baby|babies|teen\w*|newborn\w*|infant\w*|toddler\w*|rookie\w*"
    r"|beginner\w*|novice\w*|newcomer\w*|freshman|naive|innocent|jeune\w*"
    r"|初|刚|剛|最初|早期|初期|年轻|新手|新人|まだ|初め)\W*$",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)
# Words marking a start, or a first or new occurrence: a milder dip.
MILD = re.compile(
    r"\s*(first|new|newly|initial\w*|begin\w*|start\w*|just|still|yet|originally)\W*$",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)
# Opening tags of a thinking or tool-response block.
OPENERS = re.compile(r"\s*<(think|tool_response)>\s*$")


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if STRONG.match(token):
        cue = -1.0
    elif MILD.match(token) or OPENERS.match(token):
        cue = -0.5
    else:
        cue = 0.0
    new_doc = len(prefix.document_ids) < 2 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    if carry is None or new_doc:
        carry = 0.0
    total = DECAY * carry + cue
    return total, total

"""Layer 15 MLP hidden unit 4529 (read through its down_proj component), as a comparison detector.

What the component is: a single rank-one piece of layers.15.mlp.down_proj. Its input direction
puts weight 0.55 on MLP hidden unit 4529 of layer 15 (out of a total norm of 0.86), so its
activation tracks that unit's signed value (correlation 0.58 on training tokens). The rest of
its input direction is spread thinly over many other hidden units.

What it responds to: comparison and contrast constructions. Its clearest peaks come on the
words that set up a comparison ("compared", "instead", "rather", "vs", "unlike", "similar",
"same", "different", "alternative") and on the word that brings in the reference point right
after one of them ("compared TO", "instead OF", "rather THAN", "same AS", "similar TO",
"different FROM", "than THE"). Peaks reach 5-13 in the data; typical positions are near zero.

What this program does: it predicts the mean activation seen in each of those situations:
  - the connector right after a comparison cue (to / than / of / as / from / with / the)
  - the comparison cue word itself
  - anything else (the background, close to zero)
It reads only the newest token and the one before it, inside the same document.

Honest limit: these comparison positions are rare, and most of the component's variance is a
diffuse, sign-changing background that no token or local rule predicts (a per-token lookup
table, fit on held-out text, explains about 1-2% of it). This program explains only a sliver of
the variance; it is the readable part, not a full account.
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

# Words that set up a comparison or contrast.
CUE = {
    "compared", "compare", "comparison", "instead", "rather", "vs", "versus", "whereas",
    "unlike", "contrast", "relative", "similar", "same", "different", "differ", "alternative",
    "opposed", "than", "as",
}
# Words that bring in the reference point of a comparison.
LINK = {"to", "than", "of", "as", "from", "with", "the"}

# Mean activations measured on 2M training tokens, one per situation.
CUE_WORD = 0.12  # the cue word itself
AFTER_CUE = 0.56  # a connector right after a cue word
OTHER_AFTER_CUE = 0.12  # any other token right after a cue word
BACKGROUND = 0.05  # everything else


def _word(text: str) -> str:
    return text.strip().lower()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    """Activation at the newest token: its comparison situation, from the last two tokens."""
    word = _word(prefix.token_strings[-1])
    same_doc = len(prefix.document_ids) > 1 and prefix.document_ids[-2] == prefix.document_ids[-1]
    before = _word(prefix.token_strings[-2]) if same_doc else ""
    if word in CUE:
        value = CUE_WORD
    elif before in CUE and word in LINK:
        value = AFTER_CUE
    elif before in CUE:
        value = OTHER_AFTER_CUE
    else:
        value = BACKGROUND
    return carry, float(value)

"""Word-continuation tilt for layers.15.mlp.down_proj:4530.

This component is diffuse. Its activation has a standard deviation near 0.9, but no short
rule names most of it: a token's identity explains only a few percent, and the context
explains little more. The rule below captures the one tendency that shows across many
tokens. It leans positive on pieces that continue a word or compound: a CJK character, or a
letter piece with no leading space, more so when the token before it is also a letter piece
(a word being spelled in pieces). It leans slightly negative on separators (spaces,
punctuation, symbols). Everything else, and the first token of each document, is 0.
The weights are least-squares fits to the component's activations on 2,000 training rows.
"""
import regex

READS = ()

CJK_WEIGHT = 0.25        # a Han, kana or hangul character
PIECE_WEIGHT = 0.17      # a letter piece with no leading space, after a non-letter token
INSIDE_WEIGHT = 0.32     # a letter piece right after another letter piece
SEPARATOR_WEIGHT = -0.10  # whitespace, punctuation or symbols


def _kind(text):
    if regex.fullmatch(r"[\p{Han}\p{Hiragana}\p{Katakana}\p{Hangul}]+", text):
        return "cjk"
    if regex.fullmatch(r"\p{L}+", text):
        return "piece"
    if regex.fullmatch(r"\s*[\p{P}\p{S}\s]*", text):
        return "separator"
    return "other"


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    if prefix.position == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]:
        return carry, 0.0
    now = _kind(prefix.token_strings[-1])
    before = _kind(prefix.token_strings[-2])
    if now == "cjk":
        return carry, CJK_WEIGHT
    if now == "piece":
        return carry, INSIDE_WEIGHT if before == "piece" else PIECE_WEIGHT
    if now == "separator":
        return carry, SEPARATOR_WEIGHT
    return carry, 0.0

"""Version numbers being introduced for the first time in a document.

Component p-82af68dd@100000/layers.15.mlp.down_proj:4531 is quiet on most text, but goes
strongly negative on the dot inside a software or package version written right after a
name with a separator, as in `name v1.0`, `name@1.0`, `name__1.0`, `name/1.0`,
`name-1.0` or `name "1.0`. It is also negative on the separator that opens such a number
(and the first digit after it), and on the space after a word like "version" or "Python".
The dot response is silent when the same name-plus-version already appeared earlier in
the document: it responds to a version being introduced, not copied.

The program reads only the tokens so far in the current document, and keeps two sets of
what it has seen in this document (carried from step to step):

* A dot whose number is attached to a name by one of the separators in DOT_SEP, where
  the name, separator and number (plus the dot) have not appeared before in the document:
  a large negative value. Later dots inside the same dotted number (`1.15.`) get 40% of it.
* A separator in OPENS_NUMBER after a word, the first time that word+separator pair
  appears in the document: a smaller negative value. The digit right after such a
  separator takes that separator's value (no novelty check).
* A space after a version-introducing word (VERSION_WORDS): a negative value.

Everything else is 0. The magnitudes are rough averages measured on training text; most of
the component's variance is in rare spikes this program only partly captures.
"""

READS = ()

# Dot in "<name><sep><version>": how negative, by separator (first occurrence only).
DOT_SEP = {
    " v": -36.0, "@": -30.0, "__": -33.0, ' "': -14.0,
    "/": -13.0, ".": -11.0, "-": -8.0, "\xa0": -7.0,
}
# Separator (and the first digit after it) that opens a number after a word.
OPENS_NUMBER = {" v": -3.3, "\xa0": -6.7, "@": -3.7, "-": -0.9, "/": -0.9, "__": -1.3}
# Space after a word that usually introduces a version number.
VERSION_WORDS = {"version": -20.0, "python": -12.0, "ver": -10.0, "v": -5.0}


def _is_digit(s):
    return len(s) == 1 and s.isdigit()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    toks = prefix.token_strings
    docs = prefix.document_ids
    i = prefix.position
    cur = toks[i]
    if carry is None or i == 0 or docs[i] != docs[i - 1]:
        seen_versions, seen_pairs = set(), set()  # what has occurred in this document
    else:
        seen_versions, seen_pairs = carry
    value = 0.0

    # Dot inside a version number: walk back over the digits and dots of the number.
    if cur == "." and i >= 3:
        j = i - 1
        while j >= 0 and docs[j] == docs[i] and (_is_digit(toks[j]) or toks[j] == "."):
            j -= 1
        # toks[j] is the separator before the number, toks[j-1] the name before it.
        if j >= 1 and docs[j - 1] == docs[i] and j + 1 < i and _is_digit(toks[i - 1]):
            if toks[j] in DOT_SEP:
                key = tuple(toks[j - 1 : i + 1])
                if key not in seen_versions:
                    value = DOT_SEP[toks[j]]
                    if i - j - 1 > 1:  # a later dot in "1.15." etc.
                        value *= 0.4
                seen_versions.add(key)

    if i >= 1 and docs[i - 1] == docs[i]:
        pair = (toks[i - 1], cur)  # word, separator
        if value == 0.0 and _is_digit(cur) and toks[i - 1] in OPENS_NUMBER:
            value = OPENS_NUMBER[toks[i - 1]]  # first digit of the number
        if value == 0.0 and cur in OPENS_NUMBER and pair not in seen_pairs:
            value = OPENS_NUMBER[cur]
        if value == 0.0 and cur in (" ", "\xa0"):
            value = VERSION_WORDS.get(toks[i - 1].strip().lower(), 0.0)
        seen_pairs.add(pair)
    return (seen_versions, seen_pairs), value

"""Layer 15 MLP down-projection, component 4532: a diffuse, mostly unexplained feature.

What it is: a rank-one write from layer 15's MLP hidden space back into the residual
stream. Its largest read is MLP hidden unit 4532 (0.59 of its input direction's norm), with
the rest spread over many units. Its activation is dense (std about 0.38, nonzero on most
tokens) and depends on context that no simple rule captures: a linear probe on the normalized
residual reaches only R^2 about 0.25, and token identity explains about 4%. This program's
rules explain about 1%.

What this program does: it predicts the component from the current word alone.
- The word "arguments" (the key of a tool call's JSON) pushes it strongly positive, about +2.9.
- Schema and documentation words ("description", "parameters", "properties") push it
  moderately positive.
- Punctuation that introduces a value (":", '":' and "->") pushes it slightly negative.
- Every other token gets the component's average, about -0.015.
"""

READS = ()

BASE = -0.015
WORDS = {
    "arguments": 2.9,
    "description": 1.6,
    "parameters": 1.0,
    "properties": 0.7,
    ":": -0.23,
    '":': -0.4,
    "->": -0.33,
}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip()
    return carry, WORDS.get(word, BASE)

"""Layer 15 MLP down_proj, component 4533: a sign-indefinite readout of hidden unit 4533.

What the component is: its activation is (x . V_c) * ||U_c||, and almost all of it comes
from one MLP hidden unit of layer 15, unit 4533 (x_4533 = silu(gate) * up for that unit),
scaled by about 0.25. That unit is heavy-tailed, takes both signs, and its spikes have no
simple lexical or positional concept: its strongest positive and negative contexts are
code, German, Japanese, Vietnamese and English prose alike. Its value is barely predictable
from the current token (out-of-sample R^2 about 0.04), from the previous token, from whether
the token repeats earlier text, or from position (the spread grows with position but the
sign does not).

So this program predicts only what a simple rule can: the component's typical value. It is
about 0 on a document's first token (the activation there is ~0) and the component's mean
(about -0.046) on every other token. This explains essentially none of the variance, and
switching the component off or setting it to this constant barely changes the model.
"""

READS = ()

MEAN_ACTIVATION = -0.046


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    first_in_document = prefix.position == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-2] != prefix.document_ids[-1]
    return carry, 0.0 if first_in_document else MEAN_ACTIVATION


if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Quick check on a short made-up text: the value is the mean everywhere but the first token.
    ids = [5, 6, 7]
    docs = [1, 1, 1]

    class Prefix:
        pass

    carry = None
    for t in range(len(ids)):
        p = Prefix()
        p.position = t
        p.document_ids = docs[: t + 1]
        carry, value = step(carry, p, {})
        print(t, value)

"""Layer 15 MLP down_proj component 4534: a dip just after the start of each document.

Its activation is near zero on a document's first token and dips negative on the next
few tokens, the dip fading with distance from the start (about -0.16 at the second token,
-0.09 at the fourth, gone by about the tenth). Later in a document it has no clear
mean that a token property predicts (its spread is about 0.3 everywhere, and no token
identity, script, frequency or repeat tested explains it). So this program predicts only
the start-of-document dip and zero elsewhere.
"""

READS = ()

DECAY = 0.75  # the dip shrinks by this factor per token into the document
DIP = 0.21  # its size just after the document's first token


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        pos = 0  # first token of a document (or of the row)
    else:
        pos = carry[1] + 1
    value = 0.0 if pos == 0 else -DIP * DECAY ** pos
    return (doc, pos), value

This component's activation (its share of the MLP hidden state projected onto one

"""

MEAN_ACTIVATION = 0.0243

"""Explains p-82af68dd@100000/layers.15.mlp.down_proj:4536, a down_proj component of layer 15's MLP.

What the component is: a single rank-one write into the residual stream. Its read direction is
dominated by MLP hidden unit 4536 of layer 15 (that unit has the largest weight in the vector, about
two thirds of its length), and that unit's contribution correlates about 0.6 with the component's
activation. The activation is small and diffuse: mean about 0.03, standard deviation about 0.37,
with rare large excursions in both directions: up to about +11 on words inside a phrase (e.g.
"handle", "child", "mic"), down to about -10 on determiners that open a noun phrase ("the", "a").

What this program does: it predicts the component is silent (0) at the first token of every
document, where the real activation is always about zero, and its ordinary mean value (0.027) at
every other position. Nothing short tracks the bulk of the variation. Out of sample, token identity
explains about 2.5% of the variance (the table over each token and the one before it, about 3.5%),
a linear bag of the 16 preceding tokens about 1.3%, and token classes, part of speech, script and
position under 0.5% each. So this program explains essentially none of the variance; its value is
as an honest baseline that leaves the model nearly unchanged (switching it off already changes the
model's next-token output by only about 2e-6 nats per position).
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

ORDINARY_MEAN = 0.027


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    t = prefix.position
    starts_document = t == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    return None, 0.0 if starts_document else ORDINARY_MEAN

"""Component 4537 of layers.15.mlp.down_proj: a "defined math symbol" detector.

What it is: this component's input direction is almost exactly one MLP hidden unit of
layer 15 (unit 4537), so its activation is that unit's value times a fixed scale. The unit
responds to mathematical notation in definitions. It is large on the symbol that a defining
word introduces ("where N is ...", "Let G be ...", "denote X"), largest for capital letters.
It is mildly positive on a symbol inside $...$, on digits of figure numbers ("FIG. 3") and of
dates after "born", and negative on the article that follows a defined symbol's "is"/"be"
("where z is the ...").

The program reads only the tokens so far. Each value is the mean activation of its group
over the training rows checked; everything else predicts 0.
"""

import re
from collections.abc import Mapping

READS = ()

DEFINERS = {"where", "Where", "Let", "let", "denote", "denotes", "Suppose", "given"}
COPULAS = {"is", "be", "are"}
ARTICLES = {"the", "a", "an"}
FIGURE_WORDS = {"FIG", "Fig", "Figure"}

# Group means of the activation on training rows: a symbol after a defining word, by the
# word and by whether the symbol is a capital. Other defining words give the default.
SYMBOL_AFTER_DEFINER = {
    ("where", True): 10.5,
    ("where", False): 7.2,
    ("let", True): 13.4,
    ("let", False): 3.6,
}
OTHER_DEFINER = {True: 3.0, False: 2.3}
SYMBOL_AFTER_DOLLAR = 1.7
DIGIT_AFTER_FIGURE = 1.7
DIGIT_AFTER_BORN = 1.4
BORN = 2.3
ARTICLE_AFTER_SYMBOL_IS = -2.6


def is_symbol(s):
    """A single letter used as a math variable: N, x, p, alpha. Not the words 'a' or 'I'."""
    return s not in ("a", "I") and re.fullmatch(r"[^\W\d_]\d?", s) is not None


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    t = prefix.position
    toks, docs = prefix.token_strings, prefix.document_ids

    def back(k):
        """The token k places back, or '' if it is before this document's start."""
        i = t - k
        return toks[i].strip() if i >= 0 and docs[i] == docs[t] else ""

    cur, prev, prev2 = back(0), back(1), back(2)
    value = 0.0
    if prev in DEFINERS and is_symbol(cur):
        upper = cur[:1].isupper()
        value = SYMBOL_AFTER_DEFINER.get((prev.lower(), upper), OTHER_DEFINER[upper])
    elif prev in ("$", "$$") and is_symbol(cur):
        value = SYMBOL_AFTER_DOLLAR
    elif cur.isdigit() and any(back(k) in FIGURE_WORDS for k in (1, 2, 3)):
        value = DIGIT_AFTER_FIGURE
    elif cur.isdigit() and any(back(k) == "born" for k in range(1, 9)):
        value = DIGIT_AFTER_BORN
    elif cur == "born":
        value = BORN
    elif prev in COPULAS and cur in ARTICLES and is_symbol(prev2):
        value = ARTICLE_AFTER_SYMBOL_IS
    return carry, value

"""Layer 15 MLP down_proj, component 4538: a weak, word-level read of "what comes next is a consequence".

What it is: a rank-one piece of the MLP down projection. About a quarter of its activation's
variance comes from MLP hidden unit 4538 of layer 15 (correlation 0.47 with the activation);
the rest is many small contributions from other hidden units. That hidden unit is high when the text is talking about
outcomes and risks ("...will result in", "leads to", "may cause", "to prevent", "avoid",
"consequence", "otherwise") and low on some plain-description or code words.

What this program does: it looks only at the newest token and gives a fixed value by word
class. Consequence/outcome words get a positive value, future/conditional modals a small
positive one, and a few words that the component tends to be negative on get a negative one.
Every other token gets 0. It keeps no state, so it is the same at every position of every
document.

Why it is this weak: the component's activation is driven by context, not by the current word
alone. On held-out training text, a per-token average (about 150k entries) explains about 3% of
its variance, and a per-(previous, current)-token average about 4%. The word classes here explain
about 0.2% (measured: variance explained 0.0024 on eval). The component is also dormant: its
causal importance is essentially 0, and switching it off changes the model's output by about
1e-6 nats, so this program does not change the output measurably either.
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

# Words that name an outcome, risk or consequence: the component leans positive on them.
CONSEQUENCE = {
    "result", "results", "resulting", "resulted", "consequence", "consequences",
    "consequently", "otherwise", "prevent", "avoid", "cause", "causes", "causing",
    "caused", "lead", "leads", "leading", "led", "risk", "risks", "risking",
    "potential", "likely", "unless", "导致", "否则",
}
# Modals that set up a predicted outcome ("you will ...", "it may ...").
MODALS = {"will", "would", "may", "might"}
# Words the component tends to be negative on.
NEGATIVE = {"make", "makes", "running", "lack", "used", "while", "too", "it", "this"}

CONSEQUENCE_VALUE = 0.2
MODAL_VALUE = 0.1
NEGATIVE_VALUE = -0.15


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    if word in CONSEQUENCE:
        value = CONSEQUENCE_VALUE
    elif word in MODALS:
        value = MODAL_VALUE
    elif word in NEGATIVE:
        value = NEGATIVE_VALUE
    else:
        value = 0.0
    return carry, value

"""Component layers.15.mlp.down_proj:4539, a sparse and mostly unpredictable feature.

In plain terms, this component is (almost) MLP hidden unit 4539 of layer 15: its input
direction is 0.59 on that unit and at most 0.08 on any other. It is mostly silent, with
rare large spikes, and this program predicts what it can:

- The word "arguments" (no leading space) fires hardest: it is the key in tool-call JSON
  ("arguments": {...}) and code identifiers. Predict 1.9 there.
- Other argument/parameter names (args, kwargs, argv, parameters, params, ...) fire more
  weakly. Predict 0.5.
- A word written within three tokens after a negation ("no", "not", "without", "never",
  "none", "nothing", "n't") is raised on average, but with mixed sign. Predict 0.15 there.
- Everything else: 0.

Why so simple: the activation is heavy-tailed and its sign is not predictable from the
token or the nearby context. A lookup of token means explains almost none of its variance.
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

ARGUMENT_NAMES = {
    "argument", "arguments", "args", "arg", "kwargs", "argv",
    "parameter", "parameters", "params", "param",
}  # fmt: skip
NEGATIONS = {"no", "not", "without", "never", "none", "nothing", "nor", "non"}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    """Activation at the newest token of `prefix`; no state is carried between positions."""
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if tok == "arguments":
        return carry, 1.9
    word = tok.strip().lower()
    if word in ARGUMENT_NAMES:
        return carry, 0.5
    # Is a negation one to three tokens back, inside the same document?
    n = len(prefix.token_ids)
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    for back in range(2, 5):
        if back > n or prefix.document_ids[-back] != doc:
            break
        prev = prefix.token_strings[-back].strip().lower()
        if (prev in NEGATIONS or prev.endswith("n't")) and tok.strip().isalpha():
            return carry, 0.15
    return carry, 0.0


def main():
    """Tiny demo: run `step` over a made-up token list and print the predictions."""
    from types import SimpleNamespace

    words = ["Engine", "flushed", "after", "every", "use", ".", "No", "registration", ",",
             '{"name": "bash", "', "arguments", '": {}}']
    carry = None
    for t, w in enumerate(words):
        prefix = SimpleNamespace(
            token_ids=list(range(t + 1)),
            document_ids=[0] * (t + 1),
            token_strings=words[: t + 1],
        )
        carry, value = step(carry, prefix, {})
        print(f"{w!r:20} {value}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    return carry, WORD_ACTIVATION.get(word, 0.0)

"""Layer 15 MLP, component 4543 of down_proj, approximated with three word and context cues.

What the component is: its activation is almost entirely one MLP hidden unit of layer 15,
unit 4543. Over sampled tokens that unit's contribution accounts for about 58% of the
component's variance. The unit is gated: its gate is open on much of ordinary English prose
and mostly closed on code and markup (observed on sampled tokens), and its up-projection
reads the word (social and institutional nouns push it down, code syntax pushes it up).
Its output depends on the whole context, and no short rule captures it well.

What this program does: a small readable approximation with three cues.
  - Biographical-record words (citizenship, country, team, party, player, located, place,
    family, sports, ...) push the activation down. They are the words that most often sit
    in the negative tail, e.g. "country of [citizenship]", "member of ...".
  - Life-event words (born, death, died, first, history, century, won, ...) push it up a bit.
  - A digit or dash inside a birth-death year span, "(1901–1947)", pushes it up strongly:
    the largest positive activations are the years in such spans.
Everything else sits at a small constant.

Scores are modest. On the eval rows it explains about 1.8% of the variance (r = 0.13), and
its edit moves the output about as little as switching the component off does. A per-token
lookup table fitted on many rows does somewhat better (about 3% out of sample on sampled
rows), but its entries are arbitrary token ids, so it is not used here.
"""

import re
from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

# Words of biographical records: nationality, membership, team, party, place, role.
RECORD_WORDS = frozenset(
    """citizenship country team party member members player players played birth located
    location place family political sports football position station teacher administrative""".split()
)

# Words of life events and history.
LIFE_WORDS = frozenset("born death died first history his her century won lost record".split())

# An open parenthesis holding a year, then a dash: the start of "(1901–" in a birth-death span.
SPAN_OPEN = re.compile(r"\(\s*[^()]{0,25}\d{3,4}[^()]{0,25}[–-]\s*[^()]{0,25}$")

# Tokens that can sit inside such a span: digits, dashes, spaces, open parentheses.
SPAN_TOKEN = re.compile(r"\s?(\d+|[–-]|\(?)")

BASELINE = 0.02
RECORD_WEIGHT = -1.2
LIFE_WEIGHT = 0.55
SPAN_WEIGHT = 1.7


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    # Only the current document counts: its window starts at the document's first token.
    start = len(prefix.document_ids) - 1
    while start > 0 and prefix.document_ids[start - 1] == prefix.document_ids[-1]:
        start -= 1
    recent = "".join(prefix.token_strings[max(start, len(prefix.token_strings) - 30) :])
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = token.strip().lower()

    value = BASELINE
    if word in RECORD_WORDS:
        value += RECORD_WEIGHT
    if word in LIFE_WORDS:
        value += LIFE_WEIGHT
    if SPAN_OPEN.search(recent) and SPAN_TOKEN.fullmatch(token):
        value += SPAN_WEIGHT
    return carry, float(value)
